newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may sell 15 pct of bank BGZ to EBRD.
newsitem.headline: Poland may sell 15 pct of bank BGZ to EBRD.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry is holding talks with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (ERBD) on selling a minority stake in Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA, BGZ's chairman said on Friday.

"The EBRD might take up between 10 and 20 percent of BGZ shares, turning the state treasury into a minority shareholder from a majority one," Antoni Magdon told Reuters, adding that a contract could be signed by the end of the year.
A source close to the negotiations, who requested anonymity, said the sale would be for 15 percent.
The EBRD representation in Warsaw declined to comment on the prospective deal.
The treasury currently holds 63 percent of BGZ, with the rest belonging to about 1,200 cooperative banks.

A previous finance ministry plan sees BGZ being privatised by the end of 1999, when it would reach full solvency after having lost about 3.1 billion zlotys over the first five years of Poland's economic reforms that started in 1989. @
On Friday BGZ said in a statement that it had made a pre-tax profit of 294 million zlotys over the first eight months of this year and planned a pre-tax profit of 411 million zlotys for all of 1996.
Last year BGZ recorded a net profit for the first time, at 187 million zlotys, made possible by the government's agreement not to tax the bank's current profits.

BGZ plans to use its current profits and 700 million zlotys in state-treasury restructuring bonds to make up previous losses. The bank needs another 1.7 billion zlotys in capital to become fully solvent.
So far BGZ and the cooperative banks who partly own it have received more than 1.9 billion zlotys in restructuring bonds.
